newsitem.title: POLAND: BPH sees 1997 net up to PLN 33.
newsitem.headline: BPH sees 1997 net up to PLN 33.

text.p: Poland's Bank Przemyslowo-Handlowy SA (BPH) expects to lift net profit this year by 15 percent to 333.2 million zlotys, the bank's president told the financial daily Nowa Europa on Monday.

"This year we intend to gain 520 million zlotys in pre-tax income -- growth of 17 percent, and we estimate a net of 333.2 million zlotys, which means 15-percent growth," the paper quoted Henryka Pieronkiewicz as saying.

Pieronkiewicz said her bank was still mulling whether to bid for shares in the current privatisation of Powszechny Bank Kredytowy SA (PBK) and join a potential banking-insurance group seen embracing those two banks, Warta, Kredyt Bank and Polish Development Bank (PBR) .

"BPH and the other members of the potential group will bid in the privatisation of PBK if it's certain that it will be a capital investment not for the sake of investing, but when real chances to form a group arise," she said.
Pieronkiewicz said the goal would be to form a group starting out with a market share of about 11 percent.
She said BPH, which has already said it seeks to buy five percent of Warta in the latter's new share issue, would then like to gain a stake in Warta life subsidiary Warta Vita SA.
She said BPH currently had no plans to start mutual funds.
